items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: Eddie Kramer, who was the founding engineer at the studio, he of course most famous for his work with Jimi Hendrix

ctx.x: Can you recall what kind of recording deck, or what did the booth look like when you first worked there?

Oh yes, very good. It was — At the time I was back in Studio B and it had a Datamix console which — I don’t think there were a lot of them. I think Atlantic had one or two, and Eddie Kramer, who was the founding engineer at the studio, he of course most famous for his work with Jimi Hendrix, and did so many of his recordings. And it was Jimi’s studio. So Eddie would stipulate what the equipment would be and he worked with a great technical staff, a guy named Shimon Ron who was a big help in putting that place…
And two inch tape? Was that —
